correctness.rationale: For k>=2, 1<=m<k, in the inherited Euclidean embedding of edge length s, the nearest (m-1)-face retains the m largest barycentric coordinates, because the orthogonal face projection moves its removed total T equally onto the retained support and the exact residual is (s²/2)(∑removed λ_i²+T²/m). Ordered spacings U_r=r(λ_(r)-λ_(r+1)) map the sorted Dirichlet(1,…,1) chamber with constant Jacobian to a new Dirichlet(1,…,1) vector. Substitution yields the same-U joint law 2D_m²/s²=∑_{r,t>m}(1/m-1/min(r,t))U_rU_t, then Dirichlet second moments give E[D_m²]/s²=1/(2m)-(H_k-H_m)/k-(m+1)/(2k(k+1)). Derived all three fixed-m, m/k→α and fixed-k-m limits by exact harmonic asymptotics. Independently recomputed all 210 exact rational Dirichlet quadratic-form expectations for 2<=k<=21; finite checks supplement the all-k analytic argument.

originality.rationale: Kyrillidis–Becker–Cevher–Koch (2012) already supplies a deterministic top-m sparse simplex support-selection procedure. Conway–Sloane (1982) computes fixed-centroid/quantization moments, not the minimum distance to an entire simplex skeleton. Indexed SCOPE simplex-skeleton convexification concerns equal-weight Minkowski sums, a different operation. Neither known statement gives the joint order-spacing quadratic law with exact all-m mean and three asymptotic scalings.
